First, we differentiate both sides of the equation with respect to $x,$ assuming that $y=y(x).$

Note that to differentiate the $2{x}^{3}y$ term, we will need to use the product rule.

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}^{3}y+2{y}^{2} & =4{x}^{2}+6 \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{3}y+2{y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4{x}^{2}+6) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{3}y)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4{x}^{2}+6) \\ [2{x}^{3}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+y\cdot 6{x}^{2}]+4y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =8x \\ 2{x}^{3}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+6{x}^{2}y+4y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =8x\end{aligned}
$$

Now we solve the equation for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}^{3}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+4y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =8x-6{x}^{2}y \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{3}+4y) & =8x-6{x}^{2}y \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{8x-6{x}^{2}y}{2{x}^{3}+4y}\end{aligned}
$$
